items.claim: The stated reason for rejecting the internal marks is byte-false at the first of them, the row's own closing criterion is already satisfied inside its last verse, and it quotes the doubled ketiv/qere verse at its back seam with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row.
items.evidence: The row rejects the two internal marks on the ground that neither break carries an addressee or person shift. The bytes contradict that at the first one. The second-person-singular pronominal-suffix grapheme occurs zero times in oshb:Isa.26.10 and twice each in oshb:Isa.26.9 and oshb:Isa.26.11 (count: 0 / 2 / 2); oshb:Isa.26.10 closes on גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה, a third-person reference to the divine name, and oshb:Isa.26.11 opens verse-initially יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖, resuming direct address. The setumah the row dismisses therefore falls exactly where direct second-person address is interrupted and resumed - the one place in the span where the row's own criterion is met. Second, the row's closing ground (a voice commanding the community, said to begin only at 26:20) is already present inside its final verse: oshb:Isa.26.19 carries הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר, addressed to a named group, each spelling unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse each) and rendered as commands in the English, “Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.” (web:Isa.26.19). Held as a form-class reading rather than asserted, since no per-token parsing is available - but the criterion as stated does not separate 26:19 from 26:20 as cleanly as the row claims. The cut itself still stands on the mark layer. Third, the back-seam prose quotes “Come, my people, enter into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.” (web:Isa.26.20) - a verse carrying TWO ketiv/qere notes, staged as the doubled pairs דלתיך דְּלָתְךָ֖ and יעבור יַעֲבָר - with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in this row, while the adjacent row quoting the same verse does disclose them: one engaged disclosure object owes the others across the seam pair. Correct as written: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים and the resurrection splice both re-collate at byte tier in their cited verses, the English quotation at 26:19 is verbatim against the staged text, and all three setumah marks inside the span are disclosed under the right type as single-witness.

items.claim: The closing-seam ground names a frame formula in the next verse without ever quoting it, and the root repetition that hooks Isa.26.21 straight into Isa.27.1 across that seam is undisclosed.
items.evidence: The ketiv/qere handling here is exactly right and worth recording: oshb:Isa.26.20 carries two notes, staged as the doubled token pairs דלתיך דְּלָתְךָ֖ and יעבור יַעֲבָר, and the row's splice stops at וּֽסְגֹ֥ר, before both, with the doubling disclosed as single-witness; the splice re-collates at byte tier. It rests wholly on a frame formula the row attributes to the next verse but never quotes; oshb:Isa.27.1 does open verse-initially בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא, so the claim is true - but a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim with no quoted form is not engaged. More pointedly, the same verse continues יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩, repeating the root of this row's own closing word לִפְקֹ֛ד across the seam at one word-space, and that construction stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.23.17, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.27.1), so the frame that opened this cluster reopens immediately past this row's edge. A catchword hook at an oracle join argues continuity and is nowhere answered. Front edge: the row's distinguishing ground - an imperative reversing the direction of address - is already present one verse earlier in oshb:Isa.26.19's הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר, so the criterion does not by itself separate 26:19 from 26:20; the cut survives on the mark layer instead, and the setumah after oshb:Isa.26.19 and after oshb:Isa.26.21 are both cited under the right type as single-witness and non-driving.
